newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI STOCKS FALL 1.90 PCT IN THIN TRADE BY LUNCH.
newsitem.headline: THAI STOCKS FALL 1.90 PCT IN THIN TRADE BY LUNCH.

text.p: Battered Thai stocks fell in thin trade by the lunch break on Thursday as investors sold on concerns over the Thai economy and uncertain future of finance companies suspended earlier this week, brokers said.
"The Thai economy outlook in the eyes of foreigners is still not bright despite an austerity package being worked out between Thailand and the IMF," said a broker.
The composite SET index retreated 12.05 points to 623.27 on 1.4 billion baht turnover by lunch.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said earlier in the day that he would leave for Japan on Sunday for talks with Japanese and IMF officials.
An international monetary source said in Tokyo that it was possible that Thailand and the IMF may reach an agreement on the financial support package for Thailand this week.
The upcoming meeting comes after the Thai government on Tuesday announced a series of drastic measures designed to heal the ailing economy.
The measures included the suspension of 42 finance companies, on top of 16 others suspended in June.
Brokers said foreigners bought actively before the severe economic measures were annnounced. Now they are selling.
Total net selling by foreigners on Wednesday amounted to 1.3 billion baht.
All the major sectors declined by lunch break. The banking counter led the sector in terms of value, falling 2.11 percent, followed by the finance sector, which declined 1.35 percent.
Siam City Bank topped the active list, retreating 0.75 baht to 12.00. Advanced Info shed four to 218.
